The Tunnel
Back in Bengaluru. Midnight again. This time Karan Dhillon is waiting for you in the tunnel. On purpose.
No phone. Leave it on the bench. Thank you.
My younger brother, Jassi. Online betting. He lost forty crore that he didn't have. To an app owned by a company owned by a company owned by Raghav Mehra.
I've been paying it off for two years. Endorsements, prize money, my house. It was never going to be enough. It was never about money.
They have photos of my son's school gate. Veer. He's seven.
Now they want the series final. One dropped catch. One run-out. Whatever they text me on the day.
The national captain. Crying in a tunnel. And I'm the only one who knows.
And champ? He asked about you. By name. You're in his plans too.
"Then we beat him. Together."
Stand with your captain.
"We go to the integrity unit. Tonight."
By the book.
"This isn't my fight."
You've had enough of men like Mehra.
Fair. I'd say the same at your age. Just don't be standing next to me when it all falls down.
You're either very brave or very new.
...Thank you. Nobody has said "together" to me in two years.
The unit leaks, champ. Somebody in that office talks to Mehra. He'd know in an hour.
Somebody, maybe. Not Rathore. Rathore never leaked anything in his life.
A cough in the dark. Behind the last pillar, with a stopwatch in his hand, Kabir Joshi has been standing the whole time.
Squad meeting. 7 AM. Both of you. Don't be late.
Kabir Sir heard every word. And he walked away without saying which side he's on.
